notes: Said 'ayn'. Written with accents when it is the number; unstressed 'een' ('un') is the article 'a'.

examples.tl: Eén kaartje, alstublieft.
examples.en: One ticket, please.

notes: Said 'tway'. Drinks stay singular when you order by number: twee koffie, drie bier.

examples.tl: Twee koffie, alstublieft.
examples.en: Two coffees, please.

notes: Said 'dree' with a rolled or throaty r.

examples.tl: Ik blijf drie nachten, tot vrijdag.
examples.en: I'm staying three nights, until Friday.

notes: Said 'veer'. 'Met z'n vieren' = the four of us.

examples.tl: Een tafel voor vier personen, alstublieft.
examples.en: A table for four, please.

notes: The 'ij' sounds close to the 'ay' in 'say', mouth a little more open: roughly 'vayf'.

examples.tl: De trein vertrekt over vijf minuten.
examples.en: The train leaves in five minutes.

notes: Said 'zess', short e.

examples.tl: Het ontbijt begint om zes uur.
examples.en: Breakfast starts at six o'clock.

notes: Said 'ZAY-vun'. On the phone and in announcements often 'zeuven' so it is not mixed up with 'negen'.

examples.tl: We eten om zeven uur.
examples.en: We're eating at seven o'clock.

notes: The 'ch' is the throaty scrape, as in Scottish 'loch': 'akht'.

examples.tl: De trein naar Utrecht vertrekt van spoor acht.
examples.en: The train to Utrecht leaves from platform eight.

notes: Said 'NAY-khun', with the throaty g.

examples.tl: Het museum gaat om negen uur open.
examples.en: The museum opens at nine o'clock.

notes: Said 'teen'. 'Euro' stays singular after a number: tien euro.

examples.tl: Dat is tien euro.
examples.en: That's ten euros.

notes: Said 'el-uf', almost two syllables.

examples.tl: Uitchecken kan tot elf uur.
examples.en: You can check out until eleven o'clock.

notes: Then: dertien 13, veertien 14, vijftien 15, zestien 16, zeventien 17, achttien 18, negentien 19.

examples.tl: We lunchen om twaalf uur.
examples.en: We're having lunch at twelve o'clock.

notes: Said 'TWIN-tukh'. Tens: dertig 30, veertig 40, vijftig 50, zestig 60, zeventig 70, tachtig 80, negentig 90.

examples.tl: Het kost twintig euro.
examples.en: It costs twenty euros.

notes: Units first, then tens: 'one-and-twenty'. 35 = vijfendertig, 42 = tweeënveertig. Listen twice when prices are read out.

examples.tl: Uw kamer is nummer eenentwintig.
examples.en: Your room is number twenty-one.

notes: Just 'honderd', never 'een honderd'. 150 = honderdvijftig. 1000 = duizend.

examples.tl: De kamer kost honderd euro per nacht.
examples.en: The room costs a hundred euros a night.

notes: 'Hoe laat' (literally 'how late') = what time. 'Hoe laat begint het?' = what time does it start?

examples.tl: Hoe laat is het? — Het is bijna vier uur.
examples.en: What time is it? — It's almost four o'clock.

notes: Stays singular after a number: drie uur = three o'clock or three hours. Timetables use the 24-hour clock (14.30 uur).

examples.tl: Het is drie uur.
examples.en: It's three o'clock.

examples.tl: De vlucht duurt twee uur.
examples.en: The flight takes two hours.

notes: Trap: 'half' counts toward the NEXT hour. Half drie = 2:30, half negen = 8:30.

examples.tl: Het ontbijt is tot half elf.
examples.en: Breakfast is until 10:30.

notes: Over = past. 'Tien over twee' = 2:10.

examples.tl: De trein vertrekt om kwart over twee.
examples.en: The train leaves at quarter past two.

notes: Voor = to. Also: tien voor drie (2:50), vijf over half drie (2:35, 'five past half three').

examples.tl: Ik ben er om kwart voor drie.
examples.en: I'll be there at quarter to three.

notes: Plural: minuten. Said 'mee-NUUT' with the tight Dutch uu.

examples.tl: De tram komt over twee minuten.
examples.en: The tram comes in two minutes.

notes: Said 'vun-DAKH'.

examples.tl: Is het museum vandaag open?
examples.en: Is the museum open today?

notes: Also 'morning' (de morgen). Morgenochtend = tomorrow morning; overmorgen = the day after tomorrow.

examples.tl: Morgen gaan we naar Utrecht.
examples.en: Tomorrow we're going to Utrecht.

notes: Said with the tight Dutch u, like French 'tu'.

examples.tl: Kunnen we nu inchecken?
examples.en: Can we check in now?

notes: Later today, not days from now. 'Zo' = in a minute; 'later' = some other time.

examples.tl: Ik kom straks terug.
examples.en: I'll come back later.

notes: Vanochtend = this morning, vanmiddag = this afternoon, vannacht = tonight after bedtime (or last night).

examples.tl: Heeft u vanavond een tafel vrij?
examples.en: Do you have a table free tonight?

notes: Plural: dagen (long a). 'Elke dag' = every day; 'de hele dag' = all day.

examples.tl: Ik blijf vier dagen in Amsterdam.
examples.en: I'm staying four days in Amsterdam.

notes: Said 'vayk'. Plural: weken. Volgende week = next week, vorige week = last week.

examples.tl: We zijn hier een week.
examples.en: We're here for a week.

notes: Days are not capitalized. 'Op maandag' = on Monday(s). Many museums and small shops are closed on Mondays.

examples.tl: Maandag vlieg ik terug naar Manila.
examples.en: On Monday I fly back to Manila.

notes: Abbreviated 'di' on opening-hours signs (ma di wo do vr za zo).

examples.tl: Dinsdag gaan we naar de markt.
examples.en: On Tuesday we're going to the market.

notes: Said 'WOONS-dakh': 'oe' is always 'oo'.

examples.tl: Woensdag komen we aan op Schiphol.
examples.en: On Wednesday we arrive at Schiphol.

notes: 'Koopavond' (late shopping until 9 pm) is on Thursday in Amsterdam and many towns, Friday in others.

examples.tl: Op donderdag zijn de winkels tot negen uur open.
examples.en: On Thursdays the shops are open until nine.

notes: Said 'VRAY-dakh'.

examples.tl: Vrijdag haal ik mijn startnummer op.
examples.en: On Friday I'm picking up my race bib.

notes: The big shopping and market day; city centres are packed.

examples.tl: Zaterdag is het druk in de stad.
examples.en: On Saturday it's busy in town.

notes: Shops in the big cities open around noon on Sunday; in small towns many stay closed.

examples.tl: De marathon is op zondag.
examples.en: The marathon is on Sunday.

notes: For a clock time people usually ask 'hoe laat?' instead.

examples.tl: Wanneer vertrekt de boot?
examples.en: When does the boat leave?

notes: Duren = to last / take (time). 'Hoe lang' = how long.

examples.tl: Hoe lang duurt de rondvaart? — Ongeveer een uur.
examples.en: How long does the canal cruise take? — About an hour.

notes: 'Te laat' = too late / late for something. Opposite: vroeg (early).

examples.tl: Sorry dat ik te laat ben.
examples.en: Sorry I'm late.

notes: Persoon, plural personen. 'Met z'n tweeën' = the two of us. For one: 'voor één persoon'.

examples.tl: Ik wil graag een tafel reserveren voor twee personen.
examples.en: I'd like to book a table for two.

notes: Said 'op achttien oktober': plain number, day before month, months not capitalized. Written 18-10-2026.

examples.tl: Ik vertrek op 18 oktober.
examples.en: I'm leaving on October 18.
